en.title: Demographic Structure and Population Change
en.summary: PART XIII begins with demography because the contemporary economy of Mithila, Vajji and Anga is built on population structure: the number of people, their age distribution, household organisation, sex composition, education, mobility and settlement pattern. High population density can intensify pressure on agricultural land and public services, but it can also create deep labour markets, dense commercial networks and large consumer demand.

mai.title: जनसांख्यिकीय संरचना आ जनसंख्या परिवर्तन
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “जनसांख्यिकीय संरचना आ जनसंख्या परिवर्तन” विषयक जनसांख्यिकी, कृषि, भूमि, प्रवासन, शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य, सम्पर्क, डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था, पर्यटन, कला आ जलवायुक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Demography as the first infrastructure of the contemporary economy
A region without a single census boundary
The Indian census baseline and the long gap after 2011
Census 2027 and the problem of an unfinished present

en.title: Agriculture in the Twenty-First Century
en.summary: Agriculture remains the largest spatial system of the contemporary economy of Mithila, Vajji and Anga even where its share of measured income has fallen. Fields, orchards, ponds, wetlands, livestock, irrigation channels, farm roads, wholesale markets and seasonal labour networks organize rural life and connect villages to towns.

mai.title: एक्कैसम शताब्दीमे कृषि
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “एक्कैसम शताब्दीमे कृषि” विषयक जनसांख्यिकी, कृषि, भूमि, प्रवासन, शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य, सम्पर्क, डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था, पर्यटन, कला आ जलवायुक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Agriculture as the spatial base of the contemporary economy
A regional farm economy without a single statistical boundary
Small holdings, fragmentation and the scale problem
Ownership, tenancy and the operational holding

en.title: Land Fragmentation and Rural Livelihoods
en.summary: Land fragmentation is one of the central structural facts of the contemporary rural economy of Mithila, Vajji and Anga. Yet the phrase is often used too loosely. A household may own very little land but hold it in one compact parcel; another may operate a somewhat larger area scattered across several plots. These conditions create different costs and opportunities. This chapter therefore separates four concepts: ownership, operational holding, parcel fragmentation and livelihood dependence on land.

mai.title: भूमि-खण्डीकरण आ ग्रामीण जीविका
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “भूमि-खण्डीकरण आ ग्रामीण जीविका” विषयक जनसांख्यिकी, कृषि, भूमि, प्रवासन, शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य, सम्पर्क, डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था, पर्यटन, कला आ जलवायुक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Land as asset, livelihood and social claim
Small holdings and fragmented holdings are different problems
Bihar’s small-farm baseline: the 2015–16 Agriculture Census
Inheritance, subdivision and the multiplication of parcels

en.title: Migration-dependent Economies
en.summary: Migration-dependent economies are economies in which household reproduction, local consumption, labour markets and investment are materially shaped by earnings generated outside the place of origin. This is more specific than saying that a region has many migrants. In large parts of Mithila, Vajji and Anga, migration has become a recurring institution linking villages and small towns to distant labour markets while families, land claims and social obligations remain anchored at home.

mai.title: प्रवासन-निर्भर अर्थव्यवस्था
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “प्रवासन-निर्भर अर्थव्यवस्था” विषयक जनसांख्यिकी, कृषि, भूमि, प्रवासन, शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य, सम्पर्क, डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था, पर्यटन, कला आ जलवायुक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Migration dependence as an economic system
Historical depth: from colonial labour circuits to contemporary mobility
Why migration persists despite economic growth
Seasonal, circular and long-duration migration

en.title: Remittances, Consumption and Housing
en.summary: Chapter 120 examined migration as a labour-market system. This chapter turns to what happens after earnings move back toward the household. Remittances are neither a single-purpose transfer nor a transparent measure of prosperity. A payment received from Delhi, Punjab, Gujarat, Maharashtra, the Gulf or another destination may be used in the same month for grain, school fees, medicine, a loan instalment and bricks.

mai.title: विप्रेषण, उपभोग आ आवास
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “विप्रेषण, उपभोग आ आवास” विषयक जनसांख्यिकी, कृषि, भूमि, प्रवासन, शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य, सम्पर्क, डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था, पर्यटन, कला आ जलवायुक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Remittances as a household financial institution
Measurement: amount, frequency and sender
Dated evidence from rural Bihar
Madhesh Province in the Nepal Living Standards Survey IV

en.title: Education Economy and Coaching Migration
en.summary: Chapter 121 followed migration earnings back into household consumption and housing. Chapter 122 examines a different outward flow: money and young people moving toward schools, colleges, coaching centres and examination hubs. Education is both a social good and a market.

mai.title: शिक्षा-अर्थव्यवस्था आ कोचिंग प्रवासन
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “शिक्षा-अर्थव्यवस्था आ कोचिंग प्रवासन” विषयक जनसांख्यिकी, कृषि, भूमि, प्रवासन, शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य, सम्पर्क, डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था, पर्यटन, कला आ जलवायुक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Education as a household investment
Schooling, tuition and the shadow education market
Learning gaps and demand for supplementation
The transition from school to competitive examination

en.title: Health Economy
en.summary: Chapter 123 treats health as an economy without reducing it to a market. Illness and care redistribute time, money and labour across households, public facilities, private clinics, pharmacies, diagnostic centres, transport providers, insurers, medical colleges and governments. A district hospital is simultaneously a welfare institution, a large workplace, a purchaser of goods and services, and a node in a wider referral geography.

mai.title: स्वास्थ्य-अर्थव्यवस्था
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “स्वास्थ्य-अर्थव्यवस्था” विषयक जनसांख्यिकी, कृषि, भूमि, प्रवासन, शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य, सम्पर्क, डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था, पर्यटन, कला आ जलवायुक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Health as welfare, market and productive infrastructure
The household as the first health institution
Public primary care and Ayushman Arogya Mandirs
ASHA, ANM and the community health workforce

en.title: Roads, Highways, Airports and Connectivity
en.summary: Chapter 124 treats transport connectivity as productive infrastructure because it changes the economic meaning of distance. In Mithila, Vajji and Anga, the decisive obstacles are not only kilometres between settlements but rivers, floodplains, weak approach roads, congestion, interrupted public transport and the mismatch between trunk corridors and the first or last mile. A bridge over the Kosi or Ganga can therefore alter a far larger market geography than its own length suggests.

mai.title: सड़क, राजमार्ग, विमानस्थल आ सम्पर्क
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “सड़क, राजमार्ग, विमानस्थल आ सम्पर्क” विषयक जनसांख्यिकी, कृषि, भूमि, प्रवासन, शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य, सम्पर्क, डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था, पर्यटन, कला आ जलवायुक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Connectivity as economic infrastructure
Rivers, floodplains and the geography of detours
Village roads and the first-mile economy
District roads, state highways and market towns

en.title: Digital Payments, Mobile Phones and Platform Economies
en.summary: Chapter 125 examines the contemporary economy through the devices, payment rails and software platforms that increasingly coordinate everyday exchange. The smartphone is now simultaneously a telephone, identity token, bank interface, shop counter, map, workplace, classroom, ticket office and remittance terminal. Yet digitalisation is not a clean replacement of older institutions.

mai.title: डिजिटल भुगतान, मोबाइल फोन आ प्लेटफॉर्म अर्थव्यवस्था
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “डिजिटल भुगतान, मोबाइल फोन आ प्लेटफॉर्म अर्थव्यवस्था” विषयक जनसांख्यिकी, कृषि, भूमि, प्रवासन, शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य, सम्पर्क, डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था, पर्यटन, कला आ जलवायुक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: The digital layer of the contemporary economy
Mobile infrastructure and the problem of regional measurement
Connectivity is not the same as effective access
The mobile phone as a financial terminal

en.title: Tourism and Pilgrimage Economies
en.summary: Chapter 126 examines tourism and pilgrimage as service economies built around mobility, sacred geographies, heritage, festivals, crafts, food and hospitality. In Mithila, Vajji and Anga, the most important visitor flows do not fit a single category. A traveller may be simultaneously a pilgrim, family visitor, shopper and heritage tourist; a festival journey may involve ritual obligations as well as hotel, transport and retail expenditure; and a Buddhist, Jain or Ramayana itinerary may cross district, state and…

mai.title: पर्यटन आ तीर्थ-अर्थव्यवस्था
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “पर्यटन आ तीर्थ-अर्थव्यवस्था” विषयक जनसांख्यिकी, कृषि, भूमि, प्रवासन, शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य, सम्पर्क, डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था, पर्यटन, कला आ जलवायुक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Tourism as a regional service economy
Counting visits without inventing a regional total
Pilgrimage and tourism: overlapping but non-identical mobilities
The Ramayana corridor from Mithila to Janakpur

en.title: Mithila Painting in the Global Market
en.summary: Chapter 127 examines the transformation of Mithila painting from a largely domestic and ritual visual practice into a transregional and global art market. The phrase ‘global market’ can mislead if it suggests one unified arena with transparent prices. In practice, Mithila paintings circulate through many partially connected channels: direct commissions, village and town dealers, government craft emporia, fairs, tourist shops, artist collectives, non-profit exhibitions, galleries, museums, diaspora networks,…

mai.title: वैश्विक बजारमे मिथिला चित्रकला
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “वैश्विक बजारमे मिथिला चित्रकला” विषयक जनसांख्यिकी, कृषि, भूमि, प्रवासन, शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य, सम्पर्क, डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था, पर्यटन, कला आ जलवायुक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: A market history rather than a style catalogue
From domestic ritual surface to portable commodity
The drought-era paper transition and its limits as an origin story
Signatures, named artists and the emergence of authorship

en.title: GI, Heritage Branding and Intellectual Property
en.summary: Chapter 128 examines the legal and economic machinery that turns cultural reputation into market labels. ‘Heritage branding’ is often used loosely to cover geographical indications (GIs), One District One Product programmes, museum authority, tourism campaigns, certification marks, trademarks, packaging, festival promotion and even informal phrases such as ‘authentic Mithila’. These devices are not equivalent.

mai.title: GI, धरोहर ब्रान्डिंग आ बौद्धिक सम्पदा
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “GI, धरोहर ब्रान्डिंग आ बौद्धिक सम्पदा” विषयक जनसांख्यिकी, कृषि, भूमि, प्रवासन, शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य, सम्पर्क, डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था, पर्यटन, कला आ जलवायुक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Heritage branding is not the same as intellectual property
What a geographical indication actually is
India’s GI legal framework and collective rights
Madhubani Paintings: the registration chronology

en.title: Climate Change and Agrarian Risk
en.summary: Chapter 129 examines climate change as agrarian risk. The phrase matters. Farms do not experience a global mean-temperature curve directly; they experience heat during flowering, a delayed transplanting window, a dry canal, a waterlogged field, a failed fodder crop, a damaged road, a higher pump bill or a price shock after regional crop loss.

mai.title: जलवायु परिवर्तन आ कृषक जोखिम
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “जलवायु परिवर्तन आ कृषक जोखिम” विषयक जनसांख्यिकी, कृषि, भूमि, प्रवासन, शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य, सम्पर्क, डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था, पर्यटन, कला आ जलवायुक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Climate change as agrarian risk, not a weather slogan
Hazard × exposure × vulnerability
Attribution: what can and cannot be claimed
A warming baseline over the Indo-Gangetic and Terai plains

en.title: Flood Adaptation and Resilience
en.summary: Chapter 130 examines flood adaptation as the capacity to live with a dynamic river system without accepting avoidable death, repeated destitution or permanent service collapse. Mithila, Vajji and Anga occupy one of South Asia’s most intensively settled floodplains. In north Bihar, rivers descending from Nepal carry high sediment loads into a very low-gradient plain; the Bihar State Disaster Management Authority describes 73.63 per cent of North Bihar’s geographical area as flood-prone.

mai.title: बाढ़ि-अनुकूलन आ लचीलापन
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “बाढ़ि-अनुकूलन आ लचीलापन” विषयक जनसांख्यिकी, कृषि, भूमि, प्रवासन, शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य, सम्पर्क, डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था, पर्यटन, कला आ जलवायुक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Flood adaptation means living with water without normalising loss
Four flood regimes require four different responses
The basin is transboundary even when administration is not
The 2008 Kosi breach as an institutional turning point

en.title: India–Nepal Border Economies after Federalisation
en.summary: Chapter 131 examines the India–Nepal border economy after Nepal’s transition to federalism. The constitutional change of 2015 created a three-tier state—federal, provincial and local—and the first full cycle of provincial and local governments after the 2017 elections brought new institutions directly into the economic life of the Terai–Madhesh border. Yet federalisation did not create a new international border, nor did it transfer customs or international trade to Madhesh Province.

mai.title: संघीयकरणक बाद भारत-नेपाल सीमा-अर्थव्यवस्था
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “संघीयकरणक बाद भारत-नेपाल सीमा-अर्थव्यवस्था” विषयक जनसांख्यिकी, कृषि, भूमि, प्रवासन, शिक्षा-स्वास्थ्य, सम्पर्क, डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था, पर्यटन, कला आ जलवायुक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Federalisation changed the institutional map, not the border itself
Three tiers govern one border economy
Customs and international trade remain federal powers
Provincial and local governments shape the last mile
